mainTopic: When will משיח come? Warnings against calculating the קץ, the 36 צדיקים, and whether the גאולה depends on תשובה
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's discussion of when משיח will come. It first admits that our sins have delayed משיח, so years meant for him have already passed. Next come several attempts to date the end: אליהו's words to רב יהודה about 85 יובלות, which רב אשי explains, and a mysterious scroll found in Rome's archives. A ברייתא of רבי נתן then rejects every calculation of the קץ from פסוקים, and רבי יונתן curses those who calculate the end, because people lose hope when the date passes. The גמרא teaches that we must keep waiting, since ה׳ is waiting too, and that only מדת הדין holds the גאולה back. We wait in order to receive reward. From the same פסוק, אביי learns that there are at least 36 צדיקים in every generation who greet the שכינה, and the גמרא settles two challenges to this number. Finally, רב and שמואל argue whether the גאולה depends on תשובה, matching a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. Each of them brings פסוקים, and their exchange continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our sins delayed the time of משיח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the teaching of תנא דבי אליהו by admitting that some of the 2000 years meant for משיח have already passed without him, because of our sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: But because of our many sins, some of those years have already passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the earlier teaching that the world has three 2000-year periods. It explains why משיח has not come even though his period has already started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching said the last 2000 years of the world are the days of משיח. Since he had not come when that period began, the גמרא explains that our sins pushed him off. Those years were 'used up' without his arrival.
steps.whatToRemember: The plan of the world gave 2000 years for משיח, but our sins have delayed him, so part of that time has passed without his coming.

phrases.english: But because of our many sins,
of them has passed what has passed.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the 2000 years set aside for משיח in the earlier teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the teaching of תנא דבי אליהו from the previous lines of the daf about 6000 years of the world.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: משיח's time has been delayed by sin; years meant for him have already elapsed.

steps.title: אליהו says משיח comes in the 85th Jubilee
steps.stepSummary: אליהו tells רב יהודה, the brother of רב סלא חסידא, that the world will last at least 85 יובלות, and בן דוד will come in the last one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said to רב יהודה, brother of רב סלא the pious: The world will last no fewer than 85 Jubilees, and in the last Jubilee the son of David will come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement about the timing of משיח. אליהו gives רב יהודה a general time frame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יובל is 50 years, so 85 יובלות is 4,250 years from creation. אליהו says בן דוד comes during the 85th יובל, but he does not yet say exactly when within it.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו הנביא, who appeared to and taught some sages
The son of David, meaning משיח

phrases.english: Elijah said to

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב יְהוּדָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, brother of Rav Sala the pious:
The world will not be less
than eighty-five Jubilees,
and in the last Jubilee the son of David will come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֵלִיָּהוּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new source about the time of משיח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world lasts at least 85 יובלות, and משיח comes in the last one.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks for details and אליהו does not know
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks whether משיח comes at the start or end of that יובל, and whether the יובל finishes first. Both times אליהו answers, 'I do not know.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: At its beginning or at its end? He answered: I do not know. Will it end first or not? He answered: I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tries to pin down the exact time inside the 85th יובל. אליהו refuses or is unable to give more details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question asks where in the 50 years משיח comes. The second asks whether the whole 85th יובל runs out before he comes. Both answers are 'I do not know,' so the exact time stays hidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: At its beginning or at its end?
He said to him: I do not know.
Will it be finished or not finished?
phrases.notes: He means: will the whole 85th יובל run out before משיח comes, or will he come while it is still going?

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details on אליהו's statement in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly when within the 85th יובל משיח will come.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אליהו says he does not know.

steps.title: רב אשי explains what אליהו really meant
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says אליהו's message was: before the 85th יובל, do not expect משיח; from then on, expect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is what he told him: Until this point, do not look out for him; from this point on, look out for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own understanding of אליהו's words. He turns them from a date into a guide for when to start waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אשי, אליהו never gave a set date for משיח. He only said that before 4,250 years there is no need to expect him, and after that one should always be expecting him.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not look out for him

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying משיח must come right at 4,250 years. He is saying that from then on we should be waiting for him at any time.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This is what he said to him:
Until here, do not look out for him;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the 85th יובל. Before then, don't expect משיח.

phrases.english: from here onward, look out for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָכִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of אליהו's statement from steps 2-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו only meant: before the 85th יובל don't expect משיח, after it expect him.

steps.title: A mysterious scroll found in the Roman archives
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר תחליפא writes to רב יוסף that he met a man with a Hebrew scroll, which the man found in Rome's archives while serving as a soldier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר תחליפא sent to רב יוסף: I found a man holding a scroll written in כתב אשורית and in לשון הקודש. I asked him: Where did you get this? He said: I hired myself out to the Roman army, and I found it among Rome's archives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by telling how this scroll was found. Its actual contents come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll was written in the Jewish script and in לשון הקודש, so it clearly came from Jews, even though it was found in Roman storehouses. This background tells us why its words were worth reporting to רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashurit, the square Hebrew script used for a ספר תורה

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Tachlifa sent to Rav Yosef:
I found one man
and in his hand was one scroll
written in Ashurit script and in the holy language.
I said to him: Where did you get this?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: לַחֲיָילוֹת שֶׁל רוֹמִי נִשְׂכַּרְתִּי
phrases.english: He said to me: I hired myself out to the soldiers of Rome
and I found it among the archives of Rome.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another source about the timeline of the end of days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a Hebrew scroll from the Roman archives that will give a timeline.

steps.title: The scroll's timeline for the end of the world
steps.stepSummary: The scroll says that after 4,291 years the world will come to an end, with wars of sea monsters, wars of גוג ומגוג, and the days of משיח, and that הקב"ה renews His world only after 7000 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And written in it: After 4,291 years from the creation of the world, the world will come to an end. Among those years are the wars of the sea monsters, the wars of גוג ומגוג, and the rest are the days of משיח. And הקב"ה renews His world only after 7000 years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reads what the scroll actually said. It gives a timeline for the end of this world and when a new world begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll names 4,291 years as the point when the world starts its final stage. That stage includes great wars and the days of משיח. Only after 7000 years does הקב"ה make the world new.

keyTerms.meaning: Will come to an end, be finished
The great war at the end of days

phrases.english: And it was written in it:
After four thousand two hundred
and ninety-one years
from the creation of the world, the world will come to an end.
Among them are the wars of the sea monsters,
among them are the wars of Gog and Magog,
and the rest are the days of the Messiah.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: And the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not renew His world
except after seven thousand years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contents of the scroll introduced in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After 4,291 years the world enters its final stage; it is renewed only after 7000 years.

steps.title: רב אחא בריה דרבא's different version: 5000 years
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא says the scroll's statement was actually 'after 5000 years,' not 7000.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said: It was stated 'after five thousand years.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different sage reports another version of the scroll's last line. He gives a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll's report said the world is renewed after 7000 years. רב אחא בריה דרבא says the version he knew said 5000 years instead. This shows the exact numbers were not agreed upon.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said:
"After five thousand years" is what was stated.
phrases.notes: He is changing the number at the end of the scroll from seven thousand to five thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the scroll's final line from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scroll said renewal comes after 5000 years.

steps.title: רבי נתן: a פסוק too deep to measure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי נתן, who says the פסוק in חבקוק about the end of days goes down to the depths. The explanation follows in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי נתן says, this פסוק pierces and goes down to the abyss: "For there is yet a vision for the appointed time, and it speaks of the end and does not lie; if it tarries, wait for it, for it will surely come, it will not delay."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא from רבי נתן. It is setting up the next move, where this פסוק will be used to warn against calculating the קץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After several attempts to figure out dates, רבי נתן points to a פסוק that is like a deep pit with no bottom. Its message is that the time of the קץ cannot be measured, but we must keep waiting because it will surely come.

keyTerms.meaning: The end, the time of the final redemption

steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק becomes the basis for the well-known teaching that one should not try to calculate the end, yet one must always wait for משיח.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Natan says,

phrases.aramaic: מִקְרָא זֶה נוֹקֵב וְיוֹרֵד עַד תְּהוֹם:
phrases.english: This verse pierces and goes down to the abyss:
"For there is yet a vision for the appointed time,
and it speaks of the end and does not lie;
if it tarries, wait for it,
for it will surely come, it will not delay."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר, מִקְרָא זֶה נוֹקֵב וְיוֹרֵד עַד תְּהוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from date-based reports to a ברייתא that will warn against calculating the קץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in חבקוק about the end of days is unfathomably deep.

steps.title: Not like the calculation of our Rabbis from דניאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the end will not follow the reading of רבותינו, who calculated it from the פסוק 'a period, periods, and half a period'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not like our Rabbis, who used to explain the פסוק: 'Until a period, periods, and half a period.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן starts explaining his claim from step 8 that the end of days is too deep to calculate. His first example is rejecting how רבותינו read a פסוק in דניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבותינו tried to get a number of years out of the strange time words in דניאל. This is generally understood to mean the final exile would last three and a half times as long as the exile in מצרים. רבי נתן says this calculation is not correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Our Rabbis: a group of unnamed חכמים
They used to explain or expound a פסוק
A period or season of time

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'not like' do not mean these חכמים were wrong to learn the פסוק. רבי נתן is saying that the date of the end cannot be found this way.

phrases.english: Not like our Rabbis, who used to expound:
phrases.notes: He means: משיח won't come according to their calculation.

phrases.english: "Until a period, periods, and half a period."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining רבי נתן's statement that the פסוק in חבקוק 'goes down to the depths'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The end of days cannot be calculated from 'עדן עדנין ופלג עדן'.

steps.title: Not like the calculation of רבי שמלאי from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן rejects the reading of רבי שמלאי, who calculated the end from the word 'שליש' in a פסוק about tears.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not like רבי שמלאי, who used to explain the פסוק: 'You fed them bread of tears and gave them tears to drink in great measure (שליש).'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second calculation רבי נתן rejects. This time it is רבי שמלאי's reading of a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמלאי read the word שליש, which literally means 'a third' or 'triple', as a number for the length of the exile. This is generally understood to mean three times as long as the exile in מצרים. רבי נתן says this reading also does not tell us the date.

keyTerms.meaning: A third, or a triple measure; the word the דרשה is built on

phrases.english: And not like רבי שמלאי, who used to expound:
"You have fed them bread of tears
and given them tears to drink in great measure."
phrases.notes: The word שליש literally means 'a third.' רבי שמלאי's calculation hangs on that word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second calculation in the same list, after the one of רבותינו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The end of days cannot be calculated from 'דמעות שליש'.

steps.title: Not like the reading of רבי עקיבא from חגי
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן rejects the reading of רבי עקיבא, who used a פסוק in חגי to say the redemption would come very soon.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is not like רבי עקיבא, who used to explain the פסוק: 'Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last calculation רבי נתן rejects. It is רבי עקיבא's reading of a פסוק in חגי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא focused on the words 'a little while' and read them to mean the redemption would come soon. רבי נתן rejects this too. So no attempt to pin down the timing, whether far off or close, works.

phrases.english: And not like רבי עקיבא, who used to expound:
"Once more, it is a little while,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי מַרְעִישׁ אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ״.
phrases.english: and I will shake the heavens and the earth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final rejected calculation, closing the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption cannot be dated as 'soon' from 'עוד אחת מעט היא'.

steps.title: The real meaning: three kingdoms that already passed
steps.stepSummary: Instead, רבי נתן lists three kingdoms: the first lasted 70 years, the second 52 years, and the kingdom of בן כוזיבא two and a half years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the first kingdom lasted seventy years, the second kingdom fifty-two years, and the kingdom of בן כוזיבא two and a half years.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting all three calculations, רבי נתן gives his own view. He lists three kingdoms and how long each one lasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא ('rather') shows this replaces the rejected readings. The numbers here describe kingdoms that already came and went. So they are not a hidden countdown to משיח, and the end itself stays unknown. This fits רבי נתן's opening claim that the פסוק 'goes down to the depths'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces the correct view after rejecting others
The leader of the revolt against רומי, also called בר כוכבא

steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן rejects every attempt to calculate the end from פסוקים, whether it puts the end far away or close. The numbers he gives are kingdoms that already passed, so the time of the end stays hidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not add up 70 + 52 + 2.5 as a date for משיח. These are past reigns, and the point is that the end cannot be calculated.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next lines of the גמרא, which warn strongly against those who calculate the end.

phrases.english: Rather, the first kingdom: seventy years,
the second kingdom: fifty-two,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַלְכוּת בֶּן כּוֹזֵיבָא – שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה.
phrases.english: and the kingdom of בן כוזיבא: two and a half years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the three rejected calculations with רבי נתן's own reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The time numbers refer to three past kingdoms (70, 52 and 2.5 years), not to a date for the end.

steps.title: What does 'it declares of the end and does not lie' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the words 'ויפח לקץ ולא יכזב' in חבקוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'And it declares of the end, and does not lie'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what a phrase from the same פסוק in חבקוק means. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן already used this פסוק to reject calculations of the end. Now the גמרא wants to understand the words 'ויפח לקץ' themselves, which sound strange.

keyTerms.meaning: And it declares, or speaks out (from חבקוק)
The end, the time of the גאולה
It will not lie or disappoint

phrases.english: What is the meaning of: 'And it declares of the end, and does not lie'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the פסוק from חבקוק that רבי נתן quoted, to explain its wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'ויפח לקץ ולא יכזב'.

steps.title: A curse on those who calculate the end
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן reads 'ויפח' as a curse on people who calculate the end, because when their date passes they give up hope. We must keep waiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: May the bones of those who calculate the end be blasted. They would say that once the end they calculated came and משיח did not come, he will never come. Instead, wait for him, as it says: 'Though it tarry, wait for it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן explains the word 'ויפח' as hinting to 'תיפח', a curse on people who calculate the end. The danger is that when their date passes, people lose hope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not only that calculations can be wrong. When a calculated date passes without the גאולה, people conclude it will never come. The same פסוק itself gives the cure: 'if it tarries, wait for it.'

keyTerms.meaning: May their bones be blasted (a curse)
People who calculate the date of the end

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the idea that one should not set dates for משיח, yet must never stop waiting.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says
that Rabbi Yonatan says:
May the bones of those who calculate the end be blasted,
phrases.notes: He hears the word 'ויפח' in the פסוק as 'תיפח', a curse.

phrases.english: for they would say
once the end arrived and he did not come,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. 'He' means משיח.

phrases.english: he will no longer come.
Rather, wait for him,
as it is stated: 'Though it tarry, wait for it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of 'ויפח'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ויפח' hints to a curse on calculators of the end, and the פסוק commands us to keep waiting even when it is delayed.

steps.title: Maybe only we are waiting, not הקדוש ברוך הוא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן's statement continues, raising a possible worry: perhaps we are waiting, but הקדוש ברוך הוא is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lest you say: We are waiting, and He is not waiting?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן's statement continues with a worry that someone might have: maybe our waiting is one-sided. It is setting up a פסוק that answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only we want the גאולה and הקדוש ברוך הוא does not, waiting would feel hopeless. רבי יונתן brings this up so it can reject it right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say, perhaps you will think

phrases.english: Lest you say:
We are waiting and He is not waiting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a worry about the command to wait from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of our waiting for the גאולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If הקדוש ברוך הוא is not also waiting, our waiting would seem pointless.

steps.title: הקדוש ברוך הוא is also waiting
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ישעיהו shows that ה׳ is also waiting to be gracious to us.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And therefore ה׳ will wait to be gracious to you, and therefore He will be exalted to have mercy on you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן's statement answers the worry with a פסוק showing that ה׳ Himself is waiting to redeem us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יחכה' (will wait) is used about ה׳. So the waiting goes both ways, and our hope is not one-sided.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And therefore will the Lord wait, to be gracious to you,
and therefore will He be exalted, to have mercy upon you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe only we want the גאולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ is also waiting to show us mercy.

steps.title: If everyone is waiting, what is holding it back?
steps.stepSummary: If both we and ה׳ are waiting, who is stopping the גאולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we are waiting and He is waiting, who is holding it back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the obvious next question: if both sides want it, why hasn't the גאולה come?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer created a new puzzle. If no one is against the גאולה, something else must be causing the delay.

phrases.english: And since we are waiting,
and He is waiting,
who is holding it back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new question out of the answer in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is delaying the גאולה if both sides are waiting.

steps.title: מדת הדין is holding it back
steps.stepSummary: The divine attribute of strict judgment is what delays the גאולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The attribute of judgment is holding it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מדת הדין, strict judgment, is what delays the גאולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק continues 'for ה׳ is a God of judgment.' Strict judgment says we are not yet worthy, so the גאולה waits.

phrases.english: The attribute of judgment is holding it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers who is delaying the גאולה.

steps.title: Then why should we wait?
steps.stepSummary: If judgment is holding it back, what is the point of our waiting?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the attribute of judgment is holding it back, why are we waiting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if strict judgment blocks the גאולה, why bother waiting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our waiting does not seem to change the judgment. So the גמרא looks for the purpose of waiting.

phrases.english: And since the attribute of judgment is holding it back,
why are we waiting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new question out of the previous answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of waiting if judgment delays the גאולה.

steps.title: We wait to receive reward
steps.stepSummary: We wait in order to be rewarded, as the פסוק says 'happy are all who wait for Him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: To receive reward, as it says: 'Happy are all those who wait for Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that waiting itself earns reward, using the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waiting is valuable in its own right, even if it does not bring the date closer. The פסוק calls those who wait 'אשרי', happy.

keyTerms.meaning: Happy are all who wait for Him

steps.whatToRemember: We keep waiting for the גאולה even though מדת הדין delays it, because ה׳ is waiting too and the waiting itself earns reward.

phrases.english: To receive reward,
as it is stated: 'Happy are all they who wait for Him.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:18, the end of the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why we wait.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We wait to receive reward for waiting.

steps.title: Thirty-six צדיקים greet the שכינה in every generation
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the word 'לו' (numerical value 36) that every generation has at least 36 צדיקים who greet the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The world has no fewer than thirty-six צדיקים in every generation who greet the שכינה, as it says 'Happy are all who wait for Him (לו)', and 'לו' in גימטריא is thirty-six.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same פסוק, אביי teaches a new idea: there are always at least 36 great צדיקים who greet the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads 'those who wait for לו' as 'those who wait for 36.' The letters ל (30) and ו (6) add up to 36.

keyTerms.meaning: Greet the face of the שכינה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the well-known idea of the 36 hidden צדיקים in every generation.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The world does not have fewer
than thirty-six righteous people
who greet the Divine Presence in each generation,
as it is stated: 'Happy are all they who wait for Him [lo]';
the numerical value of 'lo' is thirty-six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק just quoted to open a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every generation has at least 36 צדיקים who greet the שכינה.

steps.title: רבא says the row of צדיקים is huge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי from רבא, who says the row of צדיקים before ה׳ stretches 18,000 פרסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבא said: The row before הקדוש ברוך הוא is eighteen thousand parasangs long, as it says 'It shall be eighteen thousand round about.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions אביי's number of 36. רבא describes a gigantic row of צדיקים, which suggests far more than 36.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A row 18,000 פרסאות long would hold enormous numbers of צדיקים. That seems to clash with אביי's small number.

keyTerms.meaning: A parasang, a long measure of distance

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rava say:
The row before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
phrases.notes: Here 'דרא' means a row or circle of צדיקים, not a generation.

phrases.english: is eighteen thousand parasangs long,
as it is stated: 'It shall be eighteen thousand round about'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's number of 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement that there are 36 צדיקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא describes a row so long that there must be far more than 36 צדיקים.

steps.title: Two levels of seeing the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: The 36 see through a clear glass; the many in רבא's row see through an unclear glass.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This one is about those who look through a clear glass, and that one is about those who look through a glass that is not clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash by saying אביי and רבא are talking about two different levels of צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's 36 are the highest level, who see the שכינה clearly. רבא's huge row includes many צדיקים of a lower level, who see less clearly.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about those who look through a clear glass,
that is about those who look through a glass that is not clear.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דְּמִסְתַּכְּלִי בְּאִיסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי and רבא disagree about how many צדיקים there are.
steps.terutzMaskana: 36 see the שכינה clearly; many more see it less clearly.

steps.title: Are there really that many top צדיקים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks if there could be as many as 36 top-level צדיקים, since רבי שמעון בן יוחי said they are so few that it might be only him and his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there really so many? But חזקיה said in the name of רבי ירמיה, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי: I have seen the people of the highest level, and they are few. If they are a thousand, my son and I are among them. If they are a hundred, my son and I are among them. If they are two, they are my son and me.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא questions the number from the other direction: maybe even 36 is too many for the highest level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחי allowed that the top level could be just two people. That seems to clash with אביי's claim that there are always at least 36.

keyTerms.meaning: People of the highest spiritual level

phrases.english: And are they so numerous?
phrases.notes: He means the 36 who see through the clear glass.

phrases.english: But didn't Ḥizkiyya say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yirmeya said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
I have seen the people of the highest level, and they are few.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֶלֶף הֵם – אֲנִי וּבְנִי מֵהֶם,
phrases.english: If they are a thousand, my son and I are among them;

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵאָה הֵם – אֲנִי וּבְנִי מֵהֶם,
phrases.english: if they are a hundred, my son and I are among them;

phrases.aramaic: אִם שְׁנַיִם הֵם – אֲנִי וּבְנִי הֵם.
phrases.english: if they are two, they are my son and I.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי נְפִישִׁי כּוּלֵּי הַאי וְהָאָמַר חִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from the other side, saying 36 may be too many for the top level.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 36 צדיקים see the שכינה clearly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן יוחי said the top level might be only two people, which is far fewer than 36.

steps.title: Two levels: entering with permission and entering without it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. אביי's 36 are צדיקים who enter before the שכינה with permission. רבי שמעון בן יוחי's tiny group enters even without permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: No problem. One statement is about those who enter with permission; the other is about those who enter without permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24. Both numbers can be true because they describe two different levels of צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's 36 are great צדיקים, but they still have to ask permission before entering. רבי שמעון בן יוחי was talking about a much higher level: people who can enter freely at any time. Only a tiny few, perhaps just him and his son, reach that level.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening of an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about those who enter with permission;
phrases.notes: "This one" is אביי's 36. They have to ask permission before entering before the שכינה.

phrases.english: that one is about those who enter without permission.
phrases.notes: "That one" is רבי שמעון בן יוחי's tiny group.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּעָיְילִי בְּבַר, הָא דְּעָיְילִי בְּלָא בַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two different cases (levels of צדיקים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a handful of top צדיקים exist, so there cannot be 36 in every generation.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are 36 who enter with permission, and a much smaller number who enter without permission.

steps.title: רב: All the set dates have passed, so it depends on repentance
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that every calculated date for the coming of משיח has already passed. Now the גאולה depends only on תשובה and good deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: All the end-dates have passed, and the matter depends only on repentance and good deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב says that the גאולה is no longer tied to any set date. It is now waiting only for the Jewish people to do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, people tried to calculate when משיח would come. רב says those dates are behind us. What is left is a condition: the Jewish people must repent and do good deeds.

keyTerms.meaning: End-dates; the calculated times for the גאולה

phrases.english: Rav says: All the end-dates have passed,
and the matter does not depend
on anything except repentance and good deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about what the גאולה depends on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גאולה now depends only on תשובה and good deeds.

steps.title: שמואל: The suffering of exile is enough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. The Jewish people, like a mourner, have suffered enough in exile, and that alone can bring the גאולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: It is enough for the mourner to remain in his mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposing view. The pain of exile is itself enough for the גאולה, even without תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב made תשובה the one condition. שמואל compares the Jewish people to a mourner who has already suffered enough. That suffering is enough to deserve the גאולה, so redemption does not hang on תשובה.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
It is enough for the mourner to remain in his mourning.
phrases.notes: The "mourner" is the Jewish people, who are suffering in exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: דַּיּוֹ לָאָבֵל שֶׁיַּעֲמוֹד בְּאֶבְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The suffering of exile is enough to bring the גאולה, even without תשובה.

steps.title: An older dispute: רבי אליעזר says no repentance means no redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב and שמואל are repeating an older dispute between תנאים. רבי אליעזר says the Jewish people are redeemed only if they repent.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: If Israel repents, they are redeemed; and if not, they are not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the רב–שמואל debate already existed among the תנאים. It begins with רבי אליעזר, whose view matches רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כתנאי means the אמוראים are not inventing a new argument. רבי אליעזר ties the גאולה completely to תשובה: without it, there is no redemption.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between tanna'im:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
If Israel repents, they are redeemed,
and if not, they are not redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the רב–שמואל dispute matches a dispute between תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, there is no גאולה without תשובה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Redemption will come anyway, through harsh decrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the idea that the Jewish people could stay unredeemed forever. ה׳ will set up a harsh king like המן, which will push them to do תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: If they do not repent, they are not redeemed? Rather, הקדוש ברוך הוא will set up a king over them whose decrees are as harsh as המן's. Israel will repent, and He will bring them back to the good path.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר. He says the גאולה is guaranteed: if the people do not repent on their own, ה׳ will make sure it happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע cannot accept that redemption might never come. In his view, ה׳ Himself will cause the תשובה through hard times. So the גאולה does not really hang on the people's own choice, which is close to שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings them back to the good path

steps.confusionAlert: Even רבי יהושע mentions תשובה here. The difference is that for him the גאולה is guaranteed, because ה׳ will cause the תשובה. For רבי אליעזר, it depends on whether Israel chooses to repent.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה אֵין נִגְאָלִין?
phrases.english: If they do not repent, they are not redeemed?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַעֲמִיד לָהֶן
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sets up over them
a king whose decrees are as harsh as Haman's,
and Israel repents,
and He brings them back to the good path.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אִם אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה אֵין נִגְאָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר's statement
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that without תשובה there is no גאולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It cannot be that Israel would never be redeemed. ה׳ will bring about the תשובה through suffering.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: רבי אליעזר brings a פסוק about returning
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא records the same debate with פסוקים. רבי אליעזר proves that repentance brings redemption from the פסוק "Return, wayward children."
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in another ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, If Israel repents, they are redeemed, as it says: "Return, wayward children, I will heal your backslidings."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the debate. Here each side supports itself with פסוקים, starting with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as a condition. First the people must return, and then ה׳ will "heal" them, meaning redeem them. This gives his view a source in a פסוק.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
Rabbi Eliezer says,
If Israel repents, they are redeemed,
as it is stated:
"Return, wayward children,
I will heal your backslidings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the same debate, now with פסוקים

steps.title: רבי יהושע: "Not with money will you be redeemed"
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers with a פסוק from ישעיהו. Just as the people were sold "for nothing," for worthless idol worship, they will be redeemed "not with money," meaning not through תשובה and good deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But was it not already said, "For nothing you were sold, and not with money will you be redeemed"? "For nothing you were sold" means through עבודה זרה. "And not with money will you be redeemed" means not through תשובה and good deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע counters רבי אליעזר's פסוק with another פסוק. It shows the גאולה will come without any "payment" of תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע reads "money" as a picture for תשובה and good deeds, the "price" a person pays. The פסוק says the redemption will come without that price. So it will come from ה׳ alone.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not already said; a way of bringing a פסוק against someone

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But was it not already stated:
"For nothing you were sold,
and not with money will you be redeemed"?
"For nothing you were sold" means through idol worship,
"and not with money will you be redeemed" means
not through repentance and good deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: חִנָּם נִמְכַּרְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's פסוק with an opposing פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that redemption depends on תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says redemption will come "not with money," which means not through תשובה and good deeds.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: "Return to Me and I will return to you"
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers back with a פסוק from מלאכי that clearly makes ה׳'s return depend on the people returning first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to רבי יהושע: But was it not already said, "Return to Me and I will return to you"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר pushes back with another פסוק. It states the condition clearly: first you return, then ה׳ returns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is even more direct than his first one. ה׳'s returning to the people, meaning the גאולה, comes only after their return to Him.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will return to you

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:
But was it not already stated:
"Return to Me and I will return to you"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע with a new פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that redemption comes without תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק makes ה׳'s return depend on the people's return first.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: "I will bring you to Zion" with no condition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers with a פסוק from ירמיהו. In it, ה׳ promises to take the people and bring them to ציון, with no condition of תשובה mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But was it not already said, "For I have taken you as Mine, and I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע fires back with another פסוק. In it, ה׳ simply promises to bring the people back, with no condition attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "I have taken you as Mine" show that ה׳ has a bond with the people that cannot be broken. Because of that bond, He promises to gather them to ציון no matter what. This supports רבי יהושע's view that the גאולה is guaranteed.

keyTerms.meaning: I have taken you as Mine, like a husband with his wife
One from a city and two from a family

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But was it not already stated:
"For I have taken you as Mine,
and I will take you,
one from a city and two from a family,
and I will bring you to Zion"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר כִּי אָנֹכִי בָּעַלְתִּי בָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהושע answers רבי אליעזר's פסוק with another פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's reading of "שובו אלי ואשובה אליכם"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק promises that ה׳ will bring the people to ציון with no condition, because of His bond with them.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings a verse tying salvation to returning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's פסוק from ירמיהו with a פסוק from ישעיהו: "בשובה ונחת תושעון". He reads it as saying that being saved comes through תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: But doesn't a verse already say, "With returning and rest you will be saved"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר fires back at רבי יהושע with a new פסוק. It seems to say the Jewish people will be saved through "returning," meaning תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had just shown a פסוק where ה׳ redeems without mentioning any condition. רבי אליעזר answers with a פסוק where the word בשובה ("with returning") sounds like תשובה, and the saving comes through it. So he argues that the גאולה still depends on תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: But hasn't it already been said? This is a way of bringing a פסוק to push back.
With returning. רבי אליעזר hears it as תְּשׁוּבָה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
But isn't it already stated:
"With returning and rest you shall be saved"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 30:15. רבי אליעזר reads בשובה as תשובה, since the words sound alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's פסוק from ירמיהו (Step 33) with a counter-פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that the גאולה comes with no condition of תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק makes being saved come through "returning" (תשובה), so the גאולה does depend on it.

steps.title: רבי יהושע begins quoting a verse about a despised, enslaved people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers with a פסוק from ישעיהו where ה׳, the Redeemer, speaks to a people that is despised and enslaved to rulers. Only the opening of the פסוק appears here, and his real proof comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to רבי אליעזר: But doesn't a verse already say, "So says ה׳, the Redeemer of Israel, its Holy One, to the one despised by people, to the one hated by the nation, to the servant of rulers:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע starts his comeback with another פסוק from ישעיהו. This step only sets it up, because the end of the פסוק, where his proof is, comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening describes the Jewish people at their lowest point: despised, hated, and enslaved. It does not describe them as having done תשובה. ה׳ is still called their "Redeemer" while they are in this state. That sets up רבי יהושע's point that ה׳ will redeem them even when they are in this low state.

keyTerms.meaning: To the one despised by people
To the one hated by the nation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רבי יהושע's proof in these words yet. The פסוק is cut off here, and the part that proves his point comes at the start of the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Eliezer:
But isn't it already stated:
"So says the LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, its Holy One,
to the one despised by people, to the one hated by the nation,
to a servant of rulers:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's פסוק from ישעיהו (Step 34) by starting to quote a different פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's reading that being saved depends on תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק has ה׳ acting as Redeemer for a people described only as despised and enslaved, with no mention of תשובה. The full proof comes when the פסוק is finished in the next lines.
